title: Degree-zero presheaf insertion identity
statement: Let X be a scheme, U a family of opens indexed by Fin r, G an O_X-module sheaf, and i in Fin r. Put P0 and P1 equal to the degree-zero and degree-one intersection module presheaves of the alternating Cech construction, z:G.val→P0 its augmentation, and d:P0→P1 its differential. Let K(P)(V)=P(V intersect U i) with restricted scalars and nu:P→K(P) the restriction. There exist p:P0→K(G.val) and h:P1→K(P0) with nu_P0=d followed by h plus p followed by K(z).

source.place: Tag 02FU, local insertion cancellation; Tag 01FM, increasing-tuple convention

proof.text: Project p to singleton i, identifying its intersection with U i. In the singleton-j coordinate of h, use the increasing pair (i,j) with positive sign if i<j, the pair (j,i) with negative sign if j<i, and zero if j=i. Restrict pair sections to V intersect U i intersect U j and use the canonical intersection equalities. The maps are O(V)-linear and natural. In each coordinate, d followed by h is the j-coordinate restricted to U i minus the i-coordinate restricted to U j. The latter is the corresponding coordinate of p followed by K(z). Thus their sum is nu. When i=j, the first term vanishes and the augmentation term is the unit. Check all coordinates to obtain equality. No assumption that U covers X is needed. Empty opens and r=1 satisfy the same formulas, and r=0 has no i.

proof_origin.place: Tag 02FU; explicit presheaf and adjunction adaptation by W2

lean.statement:
theorem alternatingCechSheafPresheaf_degreeZero_identity
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {r : ℕ} (U : Fin r → X.Opens) (G : X.Modules) (i : Fin r) :
    let K := cechCapPresheafFunctor (U i)
    let P₀ := alternatingCechSheafPresheafTerms U G 0
    let P₁ := alternatingCechSheafPresheafTerms U G 1
    ∃ p : P₀ ⟶ K.obj G.val, ∃ h : P₁ ⟶ K.obj P₀,
      (cechCapPresheafUnit (U i)).app P₀ =
        alternatingCechSheafPresheafD U G 0 ≫ h +
          p ≫ K.map (alternatingCechSheafPresheafZero U G)
